title: Understanding the SASSA Means Test
description: How the SASSA means test works, income thresholds for single and married applicants, asset limits, and how your grant eligibility is calculated.

seo.metaTitle: Understanding the SASSA Means Test — Income Thresholds & Asset Limits
seo.metaDescription: Complete guide to the SASSA means test: income thresholds (R96,240 single, R192,480 married), asset limits (R1.37M single), and what counts as income for grant eligibility.

contentBlocks.text: The means test is a financial assessment SASSA uses to determine if your income and assets fall below the legal threshold for grant eligibility. It ensures grants go to those who need them most.
This guide is for SASSA grant applicants who want to understand how the means test works, what income and assets are counted, and whether they are likely to qualify.
For most grants: single applicants must have annual income below R96,240. For the SRD R370 grant: bank inflows must be below R624 per month.
For married applicants: combined annual income must be below R192,480 (or R127,200 for Child Support Grant).
Single applicant assets must be below R1,372,800. Married couple combined assets must be below R2,745,600. Assets include property (excluding primary residence), investments, savings, and vehicles.

faqs.question: Does SASSA check my bank account?
faqs.answer: Yes. SASSA has an automated system that reviews bank account deposits to verify income levels. This is how they detect 'Alternative Income Source'.

faqs.question: What happens if my income changes during the grant period?
faqs.answer: You must report any change in income to SASSA immediately. Your grant amount may be adjusted or cancelled if your income exceeds the threshold.
